runningWorkouts.title: Introductory Acceleration Drive Builder Drill
runningWorkouts.summary: Structured 100m workout focusing on speed, acceleration, power, coordination.
runningWorkouts.riskReason: Maximal acceleration and sprinting put high load on hamstrings and calves. Complete full dynamic warmup and do not rush recoveries.

warmup.name: Dynamic Warmup
warmup.description: Easy jogging at RPE 3-4 followed by dynamic drills and light progressive strides.
notes: Begin very easy
Focus on high-cadence strides
Prepare joints and cardiovascular system

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 20m at target Maximum Sprint Speed intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown
cooldown.description: Light recovery jog followed by static stretching and mobility reset.
notes: Bring heart rate down completely
Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 2 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Easier version: reduced volume to 2 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 5 repetitions.

mainSet.name: Maximum REPEAT Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 5 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 4 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 180s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: Full recovery between sprints ensures maximal speed quality and reduces injury risk.
Emphasize explosive starts, rapid arm drive, and proper ankle stiffness.
Ensure full nervous system recovery; do not rush starts while feeling winded.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Run repetitions of 800m at target 400m Race Pace / High Lactate Pace intensity.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 90s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

cooldown.name: Recovery Cooldown

Perform dynamic stretches
Rehydrate immediately

easier.description: Reduce interval volume by running 3 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment

notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.

harder.description: Increase interval volume by running 6 repetitions.

mainSet.name: 400m INTERVAL Interval Segment
mainSet.description: Harder version: increased volume to 6 reps.
notes: Maintain consistent pacing throughout all 5 repeats.
Focus on clean running form and loose shoulders.
Use the 90s recovery to lower heart rate curves.

coachingNotes: High lactate tolerance is developed by sustaining high-speed mechanics under muscular burn.
Manage the race distribution: accelerate smoothly in the first 50m, then float.
Focus on knee drive and loose shoulders over the final 100m.
commonMistakes: Rushing recovery times, which degrades explosive speed quality and increases muscular tension.
Tensing up at max speed instead of maintaining loose, tall posture.
Improper starting block alignment, resulting in poor drive angles.
safetyNotes: Ensure a thorough dynamic warmup and progressive strides are completed before max sprints.
Do not push past any muscular tightness or cramping in hamstrings or calves.
Perform high-speed repeats on flat surfaces with clean traction.
